recipes.name: Window-light shadow map over a flat layout
recipes.line: Makes a flat title card or layout look as if it sits in a room with sunlight falling through a window: long soft diagonal shadows with light bands between them. Reach for it when a clean graphic looks too digital and needs contrast and a sense of place without any 3D.

section.heading: Window-light shadow map over a flat layout

recipes.name: Soft diagonal wipe-on for a shadow map
recipes.line: Brings window-light shadows into a shot as if the sun had just come out: the shadow sweeps across the layout along the strips over about a second instead of popping on. Use it on the opening beat of a title card that carries a shadow map.

section.heading: Soft diagonal wipe-on for a shadow map

recipes.name: Graphics riding a spinning real object
recipes.line: Lets a real photographed object drive the motion: a cut-out wheel (or any round object) spins, and a ring of graphic cards fanned around its centre turns with it like a carousel. Use it for a "meet the team" or product-range beat that should feel physical rather than a plain slider.

section.heading: Graphics riding a spinning real object

recipes.name: Swap a layer's photo and keep everything built on it
recipes.line: A time-saver, not a look. Once one card, slot or frame is fully built (transforms, masks or mattes, parenting, keyframes, effects), you put a different photo or clip into it without rebuilding anything.

section.heading: Swap a layer's photo and keep everything built on it

recipes.name: Seat a cut-out object with a soft, doubled drop shadow
recipes.line: When a photographed object cut out of its background (a product, a prop, a wheel) is dropped into a flat graphic scene and looks pasted on, a very soft, barely offset drop shadow gives it a dark halo that grounds it. Stack a second, even softer copy when the first is too faint.

section.heading: Seat a cut-out object with a soft, doubled drop shadow

recipes.name: Tuck graphics behind a person with an automatic object matte
recipes.line: For talking-head or presenter footage on a plain wall: cards, titles and text sit between the person and the wall, so the person stands in front of the graphics. Reach for it when overlays would otherwise cover the face or body.

section.heading: Tuck graphics behind a person with an automatic object matte

recipes.name: Key a rough, unevenly lit green backdrop with a machine-learning keyer
recipes.line: For stock or found footage shot against a coloured wall that was never meant to be keyed (uneven light, olive green, shadows), when a classic colour keyer leaves grey residue. The person comes out clean, hair included, ready to sit over graphics.

section.heading: Key a rough, unevenly lit green backdrop with a machine-learning keyer

recipes.name: Stacked white discs that grow out of the centre with long soft shadows
recipes.line: A title or opener background that makes a near-white frame look premium and tactile: white discs swell out from the centre one after another, each one raised off the one below with a pale rim and a long, soft shadow to one side. Reach for it when a clean white brand look needs depth and slow motion behind type.

section.heading: Stacked white discs that grow out of the centre with long soft shadows

recipes.name: Soft lens blur at the frame sides plus fine grain
recipes.line: A last pass that makes a clean, drawn graphic look as if it was shot through a lens: the left and right sides go slightly soft while the centre stays crisp, and a little grain breaks up the flat digital fills. Use it on any finished graphic or title plate, especially pale ones where the cleanliness gives away that they are drawn.

section.heading: Soft lens blur at the frame sides plus fine grain

recipes.name: Flat UI graphic on a glossy extruded plate
recipes.line: Turns a flat 2D card or UI panel into a solid, glossy object floating over a pale floor with a real cast shadow, while the graphic on its face keeps its exact flat colours. Reach for it when a 2D layout needs to read as a physical product shot without leaving After Effects.

section.heading: Flat UI graphic on a glossy extruded plate

recipes.name: Depth of field on a row of glossy plates (Advanced 3D camera)
recipes.line: Gives a 3D product-style scene a photographic lens: duplicated objects staggered in depth fall progressively out of focus, and a small camera move adds life. Use it to sell scale and depth once a scene from recipe 10 exists.

section.heading: Depth of field on a row of glossy plates (Advanced 3D camera)

recipes.name: Soft one-way blurred dark shapes with a bright stroke fringe on a pale ground
recipes.line: Turns two flat, crude shapes into a soft, lens-like backdrop in under a minute. Reach for it when a title or scene needs an organic, out-of-focus base layer rather than hard vector art.

section.heading: Soft one-way blurred dark shapes with a bright stroke fringe on a pale ground

recipes.name: Wiggled glow, darkest radial blur and fine grain finish for bright scenes
recipes.line: A three-adjustment-layer finish that makes any soft, light-backed composition bloom and gain film grit, with wiggle expressions on the glow radius and blur amount as its only source of movement. Use it over a blurred or abstract backdrop (in the tutorial, the blurred shapes of technique 01, whose figures are repeated in step 1) when the frame feels static and digital.

section.heading: Wiggled glow, darkest radial blur and fine grain finish for bright scenes

recipes.name: Soft pockets of light from heavily blurred edge shapes
recipes.line: Adds soft patches of lighter tone around the edges of an otherwise finished frame (with a wiggle on one blur for movement), so the dark areas are not flat and the eye is pulled toward the centre. A quick pass to make a background feel lit and alive.

section.heading: Soft pockets of light from heavily blurred edge shapes

recipes.name: Liquid merge of outlined circles with blur and choke
recipes.line: Makes separate shapes fuse like drops of liquid when one drifts into another, so a plain layout of circles becomes an organic, slow-breathing background or a morph between two forms.

section.heading: Liquid merge of outlined circles with blur and choke

recipes.name: A dark mass split open behind a travelling ball
recipes.line: A small ball crosses the frame and a large dark form tears open behind it, revealing the light ground; good for line-led animation, progress moments or a reveal that clears space for a headline.

section.heading: A dark mass split open behind a travelling ball

recipes.name: Turning a crude gradient disc into a grainy glowing orb
recipes.line: Rescues a deliberately plain graphic (two gradient circles) into a soft, filmic hero object for a title card or an event poster background, using only blur, heavy grain, a huge glow and posterize.

section.heading: Turning a crude gradient disc into a grainy glowing orb

recipes.name: Counter driven by one slider on a control null
recipes.line: A stat that counts up (or down) to a figure, so a number lands with weight. The same slider later drives a ring (02-ring-fills-to-value) and bars (03-bars-grow-to-values), so one keyframed value moves the number and its graphic together.

section.heading: Counter driven by one slider on a control null

recipes.name: Ring that fills to the counter's value
recipes.line: A percentage stat shown as a donut that draws on to the same figure the number counts to, so the graphic and the number can never disagree. Builds on 01-value-driven-counter: it reuses that recipe's null and slider.

section.heading: Ring that fills to the counter's value

recipes.name: Round-capped bars that grow to their own values
recipes.line: A comparison beat: several figures rise side by side, each to its own value, so the viewer reads which is biggest. Builds on 01-value-driven-counter (a null whose sliders hold the values) and 02-ring-fills-to-value (dim track under a coloured copy, Trim Paths End linked to a slider).

section.heading: Round-capped bars that grow to their own values

recipes.name: Icon that fills up to a value
recipes.line: Turns a flat icon into a gauge: a bright copy of the icon rises from the bottom over a dim copy and stops at a figure, so a stat reads as "how full". Reach for it beside a counter when a percentage needs a picture.

section.heading: Icon that fills up to a value

recipes.name: Map regions that fade up one by one
recipes.line: Marks places on a map: chosen regions light up in colour over a grey base map, each with a numbered list entry, so a viewer reads "these places" in order. Use it for coverage, rankings or "where" beats.

section.heading: Map regions that fade up one by one

recipes.name: A pill button built in its own comp
recipes.line: The call-to-action button for an end card or app demo: a flat, fully rounded pill with a centred caps label, kept in its own comp so the scene can place, scale, slide and "press" it as one layer.

section.heading: A pill button built in its own comp

recipes.name: A soft coloured lift under a button, and an inset label
recipes.line: Lifts a flat UI button off a white page so it reads as a pressable object, with a long, very soft glow-like shadow in the button's own colour straight underneath, and gives the label a slight pressed-in feel with two tiny shadows.

section.heading: A soft coloured lift under a button, and an inset label

recipes.name: Headline, button and web address stacked on a white square
recipes.line: The closing card of a social ad or product promo: one line of headline, one button and a quiet web address, on a clean white square, centred on one vertical axis and ready to be animated in.

section.heading: Headline, button and web address stacked on a white square

recipes.name: Tap cursor built from two translucent discs
recipes.line: A stand-in for a finger or touch point in a UI demo. It is a soft, translucent touch marker that reads on a white screen without hiding the button under it.

section.heading: Tap cursor built from two translucent discs

recipes.name: Card elements slide in from the left, one after another
recipes.line: Builds an end card or call-to-action screen in a quick, readable cascade: each element arrives from off the left edge and lands in place a few frames after the one above it, so the eye reads headline, then button, then address.

section.heading: Card elements slide in from the left, one after another

recipes.name: Cursor glides in and taps the button
recipes.line: Shows a tap on a UI element. A touch marker slides in from off screen and stops on a button, and the button dips in scale and springs back, so the viewer reads "pressed".

section.heading: Cursor glides in and taps the button

recipes.name: Curved, eased cursor route in and out
recipes.line: Makes a touch marker move like a hand, not a robot. It arcs in, pauses on the button for the tap, then arcs out and off screen, with eased starts and stops.

section.heading: Curved, eased cursor route in and out

recipes.name: Card elements slide out to the right in the same cascade
recipes.line: Clears an end card or call-to-action screen with the same cascade it arrived with, carried on in the same direction: the elements leave off the right edge one after another, so the card reads as passing through the frame. Also a pass to even out the gaps between entrance, tap and exit.

section.heading: Card elements slide out to the right in the same cascade

recipes.name: Round dots from a shape stroke
recipes.line: Turns any stroked line or outline into an evenly spaced row or ring of round dots with no extra layers, for loaders, orbit rings, borders and decorative circles around a title.

section.heading: Round dots from a shape stroke

recipes.name: Arc with a dot at each end
recipes.line: A thin line or arc with a round dot at each end, built inside one shape layer, for orbit segments, connector lines, data callouts and ring loaders.

section.heading: Arc with a dot at each end

recipes.name: Fade both ends of an open stroke with Taper
recipes.line: Makes an open stroke thin to nothing at both ends, so a light streak, horizon arc or swoosh fades out softly instead of stopping in a hard square end.

section.heading: Fade both ends of an open stroke with Taper

recipes.name: Text carousel from rotated copies around one pivot
recipes.line: Builds a wheel of repeated words (or any layer) curving around an off-screen pivot. Use it for list reveals, title wheels and "rolodex" type moments without expressions or plugins.

section.heading: Text carousel from rotated copies around one pivot

recipes.name: Even time stagger by dragging a whole stack at once
recipes.line: Makes a stack of copies appear one after another at an even interval, so items of a list, ring or grid arrive in sequence. A quick replacement for Sequence Layers or hand-nudging each bar.

section.heading: Even time stagger by dragging a whole stack at once

recipes.name: Tilted 3D ring of discs orbiting a centre
recipes.line: Wraps a central object in a tilted, torus-like ring of repeated flat shapes that pass in front of and behind it. Use it for an orbit or "planet with rings" look, or any hero object that needs a 3D halo, with no 3D plugin.

section.heading: Tilted 3D ring of discs orbiting a centre

recipes.name: Keep an orbiting 3D layer turned towards the camera
recipes.line: When a flat 3D layer circles around something (a moon round a planet, an icon on an orbit), it turns edge-on and thins out at parts of the loop; this keeps it reading as a full, flat shape the whole way round.

section.heading: Keep an orbiting 3D layer turned towards the camera

recipes.name: Perform puppet-pin motion live with the mouse
recipes.line: For organic secondary motion on an illustrated character (a head sway, a nod, a drifting limb) where hand-placing keyframes would look stiff or take too long; you act the motion out once and After Effects writes the keyframes.

section.heading: Perform puppet-pin motion live with the mouse

recipes.name: Slide a background endlessly with mirrored tiling
recipes.line: For a background that has to keep moving longer than the artwork is wide, such as the view out of a moving vehicle's window; the image is repeated and slid along without visible seams.

section.heading: Slide a background endlessly with mirrored tiling

recipes.name: Leaf-shaped particles from any graphic
recipes.line: Fill a scene with drifting copies of a small graphic (leaves, petals, confetti, logos) without hand-placing them; the particle system births, spins and moves each copy for you.

section.heading: Leaf-shaped particles from any graphic

recipes.name: Soft embossed finish for white shapes on a pale background
recipes.line: When a pure white shape or title vanishes into a light background, two layer styles give it a faint cool shading and a bright rim. On their own they only tint the shape; it reads as a raised, soft-plastic object once a long soft shadow lies under it and the shapes around it get the same treatment, so the pieces look stacked.

section.heading: Soft embossed finish for white shapes on a pale background

recipes.name: Long soft shadow from a radially blurred black copy
recipes.line: Gives flat shapes or letters a long, fading directional shadow, as if lit by a low sun, which reads especially well on bright, pale backgrounds.

section.heading: Long soft shadow from a radially blurred black copy

recipes.name: Fine dot-grid background from a ball-grid effect
recipes.line: A quick, quiet design texture for a plain or pale background, so an empty backdrop reads as designed rather than blank without pulling focus from the type or graphics in front.

section.heading: Fine dot-grid background from a ball-grid effect

recipes.name: Real cast shadows on an invisible 3D floor
recipes.line: Grounds flat 3D layers in a scene by giving them soft, believable shadows on the ground, without letting the light change the colour of the graphics themselves.

section.heading: Real cast shadows on an invisible 3D floor

recipes.name: Un-clip an effect with Grow Bounds
recipes.line: Fixes effects that are cut off with a hard edge because the layer's bounding box is too small, for example a blurred or stretched shadow running past the edge of its source artwork.

section.heading: Un-clip an effect with Grow Bounds

recipes.name: Keep a chosen layer sharp while the camera travels
recipes.line: Use when a camera push or drift through a layered 3D scene should keep the hero element crisp the whole time, so depth of field never drifts off the subject as the camera's distance to it changes.

section.heading: Keep a chosen layer sharp while the camera travels

recipes.name: Tie a 3D scene together with depth fog over the precomp
recipes.line: Use when separately made 3D layers look pasted together; a coloured depth fog over the finished scene lifts the darks and sinks the distance into one atmosphere.

section.heading: Tie a 3D scene together with depth fog over the precomp

recipes.name: Soft word-by-word rise-and-fade text reveal
recipes.line: Use for a headline or tagline that should arrive gently, words sliding up and fading in one after another with a smooth overlap, with no per-word keyframes.

section.heading: Soft word-by-word rise-and-fade text reveal

recipes.name: Text that runs round a drawn path
recipes.line: Wrap a repeated line of type round a circle (or any shape you draw) and slide it along the path, so a badge or seal of words circles a central title.

section.heading: Text that runs round a drawn path

recipes.name: Two stacked glows for a soft cinematic bloom
recipes.line: A finishing pass on bright line art or type on a dark ground: one tight glow for a halo near the edges plus one very wide glow for a faint bloom, without looking blown out.

section.heading: Two stacked glows for a soft cinematic bloom

recipes.name: Paper texture through a title matte, with roughened edges
recipes.line: Make a title look printed or stamped into a worn paper texture instead of floating on top of it: the texture itself forms the letters, brightened, and the letter edges are broken up.

section.heading: Paper texture through a title matte, with roughened edges

recipes.name: Tuck helper layers out of the timeline with the shy switch
recipes.line: When a comp has dozens of support layers (mattes, lines, labels) and you only want to touch a few, mark the rest shy and hide them from the layer stack without precomposing. The comp structure and the render stay unchanged.

section.heading: Tuck helper layers out of the timeline with the shy switch

recipes.name: Dial motion blur strength with the comp's shutter angle
recipes.line: When motion blur is on but reads too subtle (or too smeary), change the composition's shutter angle to set how long each frame's blur streak is, without touching the animation.

section.heading: Dial motion blur strength with the comp's shutter angle

recipes.name: Keep a scaled-up precomp of vector art crisp
recipes.line: When a precomp built from shape and text layers is pushed far past 100% (a big push-in or a hero zoom), turn on the layer's collapse/rasterize switch so the vector contents are redrawn at the new size instead of being enlarged as pixels.

section.heading: Keep a scaled-up precomp of vector art crisp

recipes.name: Frame video in a custom shape with a track matte
recipes.line: When a photo or clip should sit in a designed window rather than a plain rectangle (for example, a cut-out that leaves room for a headline), draw any shape and use it as the clip's matte.

section.heading: Frame video in a custom shape with a track matte

recipes.name: Rounded-rectangle matte card that carries its media and labels
recipes.line: Turns any photo or clip into a tidy rounded card whose size and position are driven by one shape layer, so the card can later be swung, scaled or duplicated as a unit. Reach for it as the base piece of any card carousel or media stack.

section.heading: Rounded-rectangle matte card that carries its media and labels

recipes.name: Card that swings round a pivot below the frame, one step at a time, forever
recipes.line: Gives a card (or later a row of cards) a carousel step: it swings in from one side on a big arc, settles upright, pauses, then swings out the other side, and the step repeats endlessly from only three keyframes. Use it for product or photo carousels, list reveals, or any "next item" rhythm.

section.heading: Card that swings round a pivot below the frame, one step at a time, forever

recipes.name: Card shrinks and leans outward at the ends of its swing
recipes.line: Adds a size-and-lean change on top of the pivot swing so the card is small and tipped outward while it is off to the side and full size and upright when it reaches the top. This is what makes a swinging carousel feel like it is "resizing" and gives the centred item its emphasis.

section.heading: Card shrinks and leans outward at the ends of its swing

recipes.name: Chained copies of a swinging card, placed with a helper null
recipes.line: Turns one looping swing card into a carousel of several cards that follow each other round the same pivot, one swing step apart, so a new card always arrives as the previous one leaves. Reach for it for product, photo or profile carousels where each beat shows the next item.

section.heading: Chained copies of a swinging card, placed with a helper null

recipes.name: Cards orbiting an ellipse drawn as a mask
recipes.line: Sends a ring of photo cards round an oval forever, framing a title or product in the middle. Use it for an endless moodboard or gallery loop behind a headline, or a hold that has to run for any length.

section.heading: Cards orbiting an ellipse drawn as a mask

recipes.name: Cards growing along a drawn path into a stacked trail
recipes.line: A stream of photo cards is born as specks, grows and straightens as it sweeps along a looping path, and brakes to a stop in a fanned stack. Use it for a gallery reveal, a "many stories" opener, or a build-up behind a title.

section.heading: Cards growing along a drawn path into a stacked trail

recipes.name: Spinning square box built from four 3D cards
recipes.line: Turns a handful of photo cards into a rotating four-walled box seen end-on, a quick 3D showcase loop for a gallery or "many images" moment, and the base unit for the tunnel in 08.

section.heading: Spinning square box built from four 3D cards

recipes.name: Counter-spinning tunnel from stacked card boxes
recipes.line: Extends the spinning box (07) into a deep tunnel of photo walls whose alternate rings turn in opposite directions; a hypnotic gallery loop or the set for a camera fly-through (09).

section.heading: Counter-spinning tunnel from stacked card boxes

recipes.name: Camera push into the card tunnel with depth of field
recipes.line: Flies the viewer into the counter-spinning card tunnel (08) while shallow focus melts the near and far walls, for an immersive opener or transition through a wall of images.

section.heading: Camera push into the card tunnel with depth of field

recipes.name: Ring of 3D photo cards seen from inside
recipes.line: Puts the viewer in the middle of a slowly turning ring of photo cards, so a gallery wraps around the frame instead of sliding past it. Reach for it for a portfolio, lookbook or "many stories" moment.

section.heading: Ring of 3D photo cards seen from inside

recipes.name: Wide-lens camera inside the card ring
recipes.line: A one-step finish for the ring of cards in 10-inner-ring-carousel: a short-focal-length camera stretches the perspective so the ring reads as a wide, immersive sweep rather than three flat cards. Use it whenever a 3D layout looks too flat under the default view.

section.heading: Wide-lens camera inside the card ring

recipes.name: Bevelled 3D text wrapped in a tiled material
recipes.line: Turns a flat title into a solid, physical object with rounded edges and a real surface (metal, stone, paint) in a few clicks; the base for any lit 3D title shot.

section.heading: Bevelled 3D text wrapped in a tiled material

recipes.name: Backlit environment light over a shadow-only floor
recipes.line: The quick way to make a textured 3D title look photographed rather than flat: one environment light turned round behind the text so long soft shadows fall toward the viewer onto an invisible floor, with a slow light swing for movement.

section.heading: Backlit environment light over a shadow-only floor

recipes.name: Shadowless parallel light as an extra backlight
recipes.line: A small finishing touch on a lit 3D title: a second, shadowless directional light from behind and to one side brightens the edges and tops of the letters without adding a second set of shadows.

section.heading: Shadowless parallel light as an extra backlight

recipes.name: Soft front fill from a point light with smooth falloff
recipes.line: Reach for this when lit 3D type reads as one flat wash from the front; a small, soft pool of light off to one side gives the faces a gentle gradient so the letters stop looking evenly lit.

section.heading: Soft front fill from a point light with smooth falloff

recipes.name: Letters tumble in from just in front of the lens, one after another
recipes.line: A smooth, weighty title entrance for extruded 3D type: each letter starts turned and in front of the lens, then swings into place in a rolling wave, so the word assembles itself without any hard pop.

section.heading: Letters tumble in from just in front of the lens, one after another

recipes.name: Depth-of-field camera on a null, pushed in through the shot
recipes.line: Add this on top of a 3D type entrance to make it feel filmed: letters close to the lens go soft, and a slow camera push keeps the frame alive after the word has landed.

section.heading: Depth-of-field camera on a null, pushed in through the shot

recipes.name: Warm-sided metal title: textured faces, plain tinted sides
recipes.line: A fast restyle of an already-built textured 3D title when you want a warmer, more polished metal read without rebuilding the material: keep the texture only where it matters and let the extruded sides catch light as a tinted metal.

section.heading: Warm-sided metal title: textured faces, plain tinted sides

recipes.name: Hollow chrome outline title: faces hidden, bevels and walls remain
recipes.line: A cut-out, stroke-like 3D title for a sleek or dark mood: the letter faces vanish and only the rounded bevels and the extrusion walls remain, so the word reads as a hollow metal outline standing on a floor.

section.heading: Hollow chrome outline title: faces hidden, bevels and walls remain

recipes.name: Spinning ring of standing 3D letters, stackable
recipes.line: A seamless looping title or bumper: a word repeated around a circle stands up like a carousel and turns forever, and stacked copies make a tower of rings; good for intros, loops and background type.

section.heading: Spinning ring of standing 3D letters, stackable

recipes.name: Found vector art, one object per file, laid out as separate layers
recipes.line: The groundwork for a lit, deep 2D scene when you cannot draw: gather ready-made vector illustrations, keep only the pieces you need, and bring every object into After Effects as its own layer so each one can later be graded and placed in depth on its own. Assumes: nothing; it starts from an empty project.

section.heading: Found vector art, one object per file, laid out as separate layers

recipes.name: One mood grade for mismatched art: Tritone plus a single-point Curves, pasted to every layer
recipes.line: When a scene is built from stock pieces that do not match (saturated greens, different palettes), this pulls them into one night-time or moody colour world in a minute, before any lighting or depth work. Assumes: a composition in which every scene object is its own layer (technique 01).

section.heading: One mood grade for mismatched art: Tritone plus a single-point Curves, pasted to every layer

recipes.name: Flat cut-outs into a deep stage: push far layers back in Z, pull near ones forward, rescale to frame
recipes.line: Sets up real parallax and depth of field for a 2D illustrated scene: the picture through the default view barely changes, but layers now sit thousands of pixels apart, so any later camera move or focus pull separates them. Assumes: the scene is already split into one layer per object (technique 01) and graded (technique 02), with Tritone switched off on the stone-wall layer so its lamp glows warm (off).

section.heading: Flat cut-outs into a deep stage: push far layers back in Z, pull near ones forward, rescale to frame

recipes.name: Depth-of-field camera locked on the subject, with a slow dolly in
recipes.line: Turns a staged 2D-in-3D layout into a filmed shot: near and far layers fall out of focus, the subject stays sharp, and a short push-in gives the opening beat life without any layer being animated.

section.heading: Depth-of-field camera locked on the subject, with a slow dolly in

recipes.name: Endless wind sway from two rotation keys and a ping-pong loop
recipes.line: Gives a still illustrated scene a reason to move (wind) with almost no keyframing: each branch or tree rocks back and forth forever from just two keys.

section.heading: Endless wind sway from two rotation keys and a ping-pong loop

recipes.name: Grass rippling in the wind with Wave Warp
recipes.line: Makes a field of many thin blades (grass, reeds, fur-like edges) move in the wind without animating a single blade: one effect, one setting, and it moves on its own.

section.heading: Grass rippling in the wind with Wave Warp

recipes.name: Leaves blown across the frame with textured particles
recipes.line: Sells wind in an illustrated scene by sending a steady trickle of tumbling leaves across it from one side, without animating a single leaf by hand. Assumes a finished, graded 2D scene in a 3D comp with a camera (techniques 02–04) and the scene's Tritone plus Curves grade on a layer to copy from.

section.heading: Leaves blown across the frame with textured particles

recipes.name: Rain slanted to match the wind
recipes.line: Adds weather on top of a wind-animated scene so the motion has a reason, with the rain leaning the same way everything else is blowing. Assumes a scene that already moves in one wind direction (techniques 05–07; here the leaves enter from the left edge).

section.heading: Rain slanted to match the wind

recipes.name: Film-stock grain and mood finish on a top adjustment layer
recipes.line: The last pass on an illustrated shot: real-film grain, one last overall curve, and an optional posterize for a rougher look, all in one layer over everything. Assumes the full scene is built beneath (techniques 01–09).

section.heading: Film-stock grain and mood finish on a top adjustment layer

recipes.name: Long-lens close-up that matches the wide shot
recipes.line: Assumes a finished wide scene already exists with separate 2D layers, a cold grade on each (Tritone + Curves, technique 02), a 3D camera with depth of field (04), sway on trees (05), rain and finishing adjustment layers (08, 10). Cut from an established wide scene to a close-up of the character without building a new world: reuse the wide shot's backdrop pieces, camera and finishing layers, and push the backdrop very deep so the close-up reads as shot on a long lens.

section.heading: Long-lens close-up that matches the wide shot

recipes.name: Side-light a face with a matted Curves layer
recipes.line: Assumes a close-up with the character on its own layer (or pre-comp) under a scene grade (techniques 11 and 12). Adds a soft wash of differently coloured light to one side of the face and hair only, so a flat close-up gains a light direction without touching the background.

section.heading: Side-light a face with a matted Curves layer

recipes.name: Two-colour phase bar that draws on segment after segment
recipes.line: A process or timeline beat ("first this phase, then that one"): one straight bar split into coloured phases that fill left to right, the second phase starting just as the first slows down, with step pictures lined up underneath.

section.heading: Two-colour phase bar that draws on segment after segment

recipes.name: Labels that rise out of their own bar segment
recipes.line: Names each phase of a progress bar as that phase fills: the word slides up out of the bar as if it was tucked behind it, timed to its segment.

section.heading: Labels that rise out of their own bar segment

recipes.name: Step pictures that pop in one after another with a small bounce
recipes.line: Brings in a row of step pictures under a timeline one by one, each growing from nothing with a slight overshoot and settle, so the eye walks the process left to right.

section.heading: Step pictures that pop in one after another with a small bounce

recipes.name: Small swept-head arrow that draws itself between steps
recipes.line: Ties a row of step images into a process: a tiny arrow draws itself between each pair just as the next step appears, so the eye is led left to right one step at a time.

section.heading: Small swept-head arrow that draws itself between steps

recipes.name: Stepped jitter and black-and-white photos for a hand-made finish
recipes.line: Takes a clean, flat infographic and gives it a cut-out, stop-motion feel: photos go monochrome, each one twitches on its own a few times a second, the whole frame shakes slightly and all motion steps at a low frame rate. Reach for it when a data beat looks too slick or digital.

section.heading: Stepped jitter and black-and-white photos for a hand-made finish

recipes.name: Faint graph-paper backdrop
recipes.line: Swaps a plain black ground for an off-white sheet ruled with tiny pale-blue squares, like school exercise paper, so a flat infographic reads as hand-made and educational rather than digital.

section.heading: Faint graph-paper backdrop

recipes.name: Bar chart of thick strokes that grow up in a ladder, with value labels sliding in beside them
recipes.line: A quick "how big is each one" moment: four bars rise one after another from a shared baseline, left to right, tallest first, while each value label slides in from the left. Use it when a narrated figure needs a chart that builds as the voice lists the numbers.

section.heading: Bar chart of thick strokes that grow up in a ladder, with value labels sliding in beside them

recipes.name: Chart baseline that draws outward from its middle
recipes.line: Opens a chart (or any divider) with a line that grows out to both ends at once from its centre, a calm, balanced first move before the data arrives.

section.heading: Chart baseline that draws outward from its middle

recipes.name: Faint grid held inside the chart's box, and the whole chart stepped to 12 fps
recipes.line: Gives a bar chart a quiet graph-paper backing that stops at the chart's edges, and a slightly hand-made, stepped motion, so a plain data beat reads as designed rather than default.

section.heading: Faint grid held inside the chart's box, and the whole chart stepped to 12 fps

recipes.name: Pie chart from one fat stroke, with the share pushed out
recipes.line: A single-statistic beat ("X % of all ..."): a pie sweeps round from twelve o'clock, then the highlighted share slides out from the centre so the number has a piece to point at.

section.heading: Pie chart from one fat stroke, with the share pushed out

recipes.name: Value label that rises in one word at a time
recipes.line: Puts a short stat sentence next to a chart's highlighted piece ("18% of all ..."). The words pop up one after another two frames apart, so the line reads as it lands.

section.heading: Value label that rises in one word at a time

recipes.name: Photo pyramid that dips, then splits into tiers to reveal labels
recipes.line: A hierarchy or "levels" beat. A real-looking pyramid sits whole, gathers itself, then pulls apart into three tiers, and a label appears in each opening gap.

section.heading: Photo pyramid that dips, then splits into tiers to reveal labels

recipes.name: Cut mid-move to a close-up, carried by a shared upward drift
recipes.line: Moves from an overview to a detail without a visible transition. At the fastest moment of an animation, the shot cuts to a doubled-size view of the same animation. Both shots drift upward through the cut, so the eye reads one continuous move. A later slide down then visits the next detail.

section.heading: Cut mid-move to a close-up, carried by a shared upward drift

recipes.name: Pinned instant photos swaying on a grey map
recipes.line: Marks a few places on a map with small pinned instant photos that hang and sway a little, so a travel or "where it happened" beat feels hand-made and alive while the camera holds or moves over it.

section.heading: Pinned instant photos swaying on a grey map

recipes.name: Ink-blend place highlights and a self-drawing border on a grey map
recipes.line: Points at a region on an old map with soft coloured blobs that look printed into the paper, and draws a country's outline on cue, for "here is where it happened" beats in a travel or history piece.

section.heading: Ink-blend place highlights and a self-drawing border on a grey map
